Not every dog can do this, and not every trainer can or should. With the owners' permission, I used Bishop to help communicate a lesson to Ryder. Dogs naturally understand other dogs better than they understand us. The goal wasn't to make Ryder love every dog she sees-it was to teach her that she doesn't need to react to every dog she sees. Before training, a simple neighborhood walk was nearly impossible. Seeing another dog meant lunging, pulling, and trying to start conflict. Through obedience work and carefully controlled sessions with Bishop, Ryder learned a valuable lesson: not every dog is a threat, and not every situation requires a reaction. Also notice how Bishop's corrections increase in intensity throughout the video. He starts with the minimum amount of pressure necessary and only escalates when Ryder chooses not to listen. That's how dogs naturally communicate with one another. Will I tell these owners to take her to a dog park and expect her to be everyone's best friend? Absolutely not. But can we give her a better quality of life by helping her calmly walk past another dog across the street? Absolutely. Not every dog needs this type of training, but some dogs can benefit tremendously from it. apparently i’m back in my homemade In my coffee syrup era 🤎 today i restocked my coffee bar with creamy vanilla bean, irish cream, biscoff cookie butter and toasted marshmallow. four completely different flavors, i don’t know which one i’m most excited about. which one would you try first? 4 homemade coffee syrups each recipe makes approximately one 375 ml bottle. creamy vanilla bean 1 cup water ¾ cup granulated sugar 1 to 2 tablespoons sweetened condensed milk 1 tablespoon vanilla bean paste pinch of salt add the water and sugar to a saucepan. bring to a gentle simmer and cook until the sugar is completely dissolved and the syrup has slightly thickened. remove from the heat and whisk in the sweetened condensed milk, vanilla bean paste and salt. let cool before bottling. irish cream 1 cup water ¾ cup granulated sugar 1 tablespoon cocoa powder 1 tablespoon instant espresso powder 1 teaspoon vanilla pinch of salt whisk the sugar, cocoa powder and espresso powder together in a saucepan. slowly whisk in a small amount of the water until smooth, then gradually whisk in the remaining water. bring to a gentle simmer and cook until the sugar is dissolved and the syrup has slightly thickened. remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla and salt. let cool before bottling. biscoff cookie butter 1 cup water 1 cup brown sugar ½ cup biscoff cookie butter vanilla pinch of salt add the water and brown sugar to a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer. cook until the sugar is completely dissolved, then whisk in the biscoff cookie butter until smooth. remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla and salt. let cool before bottling. toasted marshmallow 1 cup water 1 cup granulated sugar 10 large marshmallows vanilla pinch of salt toast the marshmallows until deeply golden. add the water and sugar to a saucepan and simmer until the sugar is completely dissolved. remove from the heat and whisk in the toasted marshmallows until melted and smooth. stir in the vanilla and salt. let cool before bottling. keep refrigerated if the syrups have fruit or sweeten condensed milk in them otherwise they can be on the counter  #homem#homemadecoffeesyrupe#coffeetokb#homebaristae#coffeebarcoffee
